#2694. Fantasy Basketball Rankings (Points leagues): Early-season surprises climb in rest-of-season value

Here is the points-league version of my weekly risers and fallers list. Rankings are for rest-of-season points leagues, blending recent performance with what I expect going forward and accounting for injuries, so some fallers rank above their numbers (I expect a bounce back) and some hot starters below theirs (I expect regression). Let's get into it!

This one is almost all scoring. Dosunmu is at 21.9 points over his last seven games but only 3.1 rebounds and 2.7 assists. On the season, he's at 18.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 15 games, filling in admirably for Anthony Edwards. He's averaging 32.27 FPPG, good for 67th in points leagues. Since Edwards will be out for a couple of months, the scoring and production should stick. I have him 63rd, and while that's growth, his efficiency isn't factored in, so if you trade for him, make sure it's in 9-cat formats.

The return of Jalen Suggs isn't phasing Black's production. Black is providing a mix of rebounds, assists, points and stocks, elevating him to a top-50 asset in points leagues. He's been Orlando's second-best player, an unexpected turn considering the Magic declined his team option earlier this season. Paolo Banchero could return by December, which would surely impact his numbers. For now, fantasy managers should enjoy the pace he's on for a career year, averaging 36.24 FPPG.

The second-year forward has stepped up over the past week, averaging 18-10-5 with almost 2 stocks per game. He's averaging 33.81 FPPG this season, with his rebounding being the real differentiator in his fantasy value for points leagues. He's up to 8.8 a night, and second on the team behind Cameron Boozer. I can see his rank holding long term because he touches multiple categories despite seeing under 20% usage.

Fears just gave us a look at his ceiling. He posted a 19-10-10 triple-double on Monday. He's started in every game for the Pelicans with a strong 25.6% usage rate. Dejounte Murray's trade request puts Fears in the lead guard role, and he already leads New Orleans in assists at 5.5 a game. Over his last eight, he's at 17.9 points, 6.1 assists and 5.4 rebounds. I have him 78th, and he should keep climbing with Murray likely playing his last game for New Orleans. If you can buy, do it.

Wagner is on a tear right now, averaging 28.7 points, 9.2 assists and 7.7 rebounds on 51% shooting. He's fifth in the NBA in assists at 8.3 a game and second in the league in minutes played at 36.8 and carrying a hefty 30.4% usage rate. His 4.3 turnovers cost him a few points a night, but his assists more than make up for it. I have him 21st, up from 39th. It'll be interesting to see how point Franz and the Magic offense looks when Paolo returns.

Murray asked the Pelicans for a trade on Nov. 13 and sat that night with a "left ankle sprain". His agent, Rich Paul, is already on the campaign trail, trying to get Murray to a contender. I doubt we'll see him play for the Pelicans again, as they've been better off without him. His trade value is pretty low, so fantasy managers will likely have to hold or include him in a multi-player package at a discount. In his last five games, he's at 10.0 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists, with his usage trending down to 20% this season. Even a trade doesn't guarantee he'll be better, as ESPN's Brian Windhorst says he's viewed as a distressed asset.

It's been a rough stretch for Hart, posting 6.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists through 11 games, down from 12-7-5 last year in almost the same minutes (29.8, versus 30.2). The last 14 days are the worst of it: 4.5 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.8 points in four games. His 12.6% usage rate is his lowest in four seasons and one of the lowest in the league for a 30-minute player. I have him 105th, down from 80th. Drop him in 10-team leagues and hold him in deeper ones since his rebounds, assists and steals are still valuable for fantasy. He also won't shoot 34% all season.

I dropped Green in a 12-team points league and I have no regrets. His fantasy value is contingent on his scoring and he's averaging a disappointing 12.5 points over his last 8 games, with just 3.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists. He's playing a shade over 26 minutes a night, shooting below his career numbers with no sign of a course correction in sight. I'm at 134th, down from 110th. Hold only in 14-team or deeper leagues, but he looks like he's losing his grip on his role with this team.

Pritchard and White are putting up almost the same line, and neither is a points-league difference-maker. Pritchard is at 13.9 points, 4.4 assists and 3.4 rebounds over seven games (13.6, 3.9 and 3.2 on the season). His 21% usage rate is consistent with last season. The difference has been his shot profile. He's taking two fewer shots per game, but he's getting up 3s at a 7% higher rate than last year. His assist rate is also down, so it's likely still an adjustment period with Tatum taking on more playmaking. I'd buy low.

White is down 21 spots, and it's a floor-without-a-ceiling problem. He's at 14.3 points, 4.7 assists and 2.9 rebounds over seven games and 12.7 points, 4.8 rebound and 3.0 assists on the season, with a 19.5% usage rate that leaves little room to grow. Like Pritchard, his shot volume is down and it's led to his scoring dropping from nearly 17 to 13 points per game. The stocks aren't as prevalent either, which has been his hallmark.  I have him 87th, down from 66th. Hold, but I wouldn't count on more in points leagues. He's always been a player who is better suited for 9-cat.

#2684. Tre’Davious White to the rescue? Bills’ battered secondary may need a familiar face

There were a couple of surprises on the Buffalo Bills' first injury report of Week 11, with the team beginning practice on Wednesday for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.

None of the starting offensive linemen were sidelined today. Well, that's not entirely accurate — right guard O'Cyrus Torrence, the only lineman not dealing with an injury last week, was on Wednesday's report, but for personal reasons rather than an injury.

But the rest of the surprises on today's report? They weren't of the fun variety.

None of these are particularly surprising. Maybe Kincaid. The Bills' top tight end seems to be playing some version of "Spin the Wheel" when it comes to injuries this season. Weeks 8 and 9, it was a chest injury. Last week, it was an ankle. Now he's keeping the ankle ailment and adding a thumb injury to go with it for Week 11.

Otherwise, these injuries were evident during Sunday's game, so it's no surprise that any of the players listed here are getting another day — or three — off.

Here, we have the group that decided to surprise this week. None of them were on last week's injury list, so the injuries all came during or after Sunday's game at MetLife Stadium. That turf is unforgiving, but not all of these may have happened on game day.

We did see Hooker coming out of the medical tent Sunday, but never got any confirmation from the Bills as to why. Now we know it had something to do with his knee.

We saw Bishop getting attention from trainers on the sideline. He was seen wincing as they manipulated his arm.

It's Hamlin that gives us reason to pause. It's not great that the Bills have three injured safeties. Plus Hamlin has spent significant snaps replacing Alford, who's dealing with a concussion right now, at nickel.

The Bills thought they solved their defensive back problem. They cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson, signed Amani Hooker, got Dee Alford back from an injury, discovered versatility in Damar Hamlin, and found that rookie Davison Igbinosun was doing well at boundary corner.

Now they're suddenly facing a shortage once again. Hamlin and Christian Benford aren't a lock to play Sunday. Alford has to work through the league's concussion protocol. And, if they do play, Bishop and Hooker may not be full speed.

The current uninjured Buffalo secondary would look like Jordan Hancock at NCB, Sam Franklin, Jr. and Jalon Kilgore at safety; Maxwell Hairston and Igbinosun on the boundaries.

The answer may just be a veteran. Today, Brady said that Tre'Davious White was brought in to help this team win. On Monday, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said that he feels White is ready to step up if needed.

#2681. Dodgers suffer unexpected loss as reliever undergoes Tommy John surgery

Last week, Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said the team wasn't expecting any other players to have surgery this offseason.

But on Wednesday, some more unexpected injury news emerged.

Right-handed reliever Seth Halvorsen underwent a Tommy John procedure that will sideline him for all of 2027, the club announced. The operation marks the latest setback for Halvorsen, a hard-throwing 26-year-old who has a career ERA of 4.78 in 86 big-league appearances.

Seth Halvorsen of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitches against the Kansas City Royals during a game at Dodger Stadium on Aug. 11, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images

A former seventh-round pick of the Rockies, Halvorsen was acquired by the Dodgers a few weeks before this year's trade deadline for prospects Nick Frasso and Landyn Vidourek. The hope was that he would be a diamond-in-the-rough addition, similar to Will Klein's emergence the season before.

Instead, Halvorsen struggled in 11 appearances with the team, giving up nine earned runs while striking out six batters. While he pitched better for the team's Triple-A affiliate, going 10 outings without allowing an earned run, he wasn't in the picture for its playoff roster.

Halvorsen might have had a renewed pathway to big-league opportunities in 2027, with several key relievers –– including Evan Phillips, who has since signed with the Braves –– hitting the free agent market this winter.

But now, he will spend all of next year rehabbing instead.

Seth Halvorsen of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitches against the Cincinnati Reds in Cincinnati, Sept. 16, 2026. Getty Images

He remains under team control through 2031.

Halvorsen becomes the third Dodgers player to undergo surgery since the end of the season, joining Klein (who had loose bodies removed from his elbow) and catcher Dalton Rushing (who had an internal brace procedure in his elbow). Where: Golden 1 Center — Sacramento, California

Watch: Arizona's Family 3TV, Arizona's Family Sports, NBATV

The Phoenix Suns roll into Sacramento with five wins in their last seven games, while Sacramento comes in on a six-game losing streak. For the Suns, this game is all about building off of their best performance of the season against the Denver Nuggets Monday night. In that game, the Suns' 4 main starters all scored above 15 points, which is just the second time they have done that this season. Even more importantly, the second-half energy and defensive intensity were the best minutes they have played together. Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green both looked as confident and aggressive as they have all season, without disrupting the flow of everyone else on the floor.

Jordan Ott made some rotation adjustments against Denver that worked well, and against a Kings team that is the bottom of the barrel in the NBA, look for him to tinker with lineups even more. Do we see more Koa Peat after he only played one minute against the Nuggets?

Precious Achiuwa — QUESTIONABLE (Lower Leg Contusion)

De'Andre Hunter — QUESTIONABLE (Left Hip Soreness)

Maxime Raynaud — OUT (Right Patella Subluxation)

Ben Simmons — OUT (Right Achilles Tendon)

The Phoenix Suns are going up against a rookie point guard in Darius Acuff Jr., who loves to shoot and is averaging over four turnovers per game. These are the two worst rebounding teams in the NBA, so it is an opportunity for the Suns to show they are a steadily improving rebounding team against a team that does not rebound well. The Kings bench is 29th in bench scoring this season while the Suns are seventh and only getting better. Luke Kennard, Collin Gillespie, and Jordan Goodwin are shooting the ball at an elite level so far this season, and if they continue to play well, the Suns can rely on them to put this game out of reach by the fourth quarter.

Against a team the Suns are far more talented than, the key is to play with the same energy and defensive effort they showed against the Nuggets. That level of play set the new standard for how this starting group should play, and if both the starters and the bench show up and take care of business, this game will be over long before the 48 minutes of game time are done.

#2668. The longest single-opponent winning streaks in Knicks history

As mentioned on last night's broadcast, it's hard to believe such a dominant stretch existed against a longtime rival that has been the Eastern Conference's banner of success for generations.

Simply, the sport is cyclical, and the few times the Celtics were in the doldrums, the Knicks were contending for titles. Through the many dark ages of Knicks history, the Celtics dominated. It's why they've only faced off in the postseason three times in the last 35 years.

From 1965-67, the Celtics won 21 in a row against the Knicks in the heart of the Bill Russell era. It took 25 years to return the favor.

On January 10, 1993, the Celtics outlasted the Knicks at TD Garden in a 100-97 win. They wouldn't win another game in this rivalry for over five years.

The Celtics won 48 games in 1992-93, but quickly fell into the East's cellar. They wouldn't win 40 games again in a season until 2001-02, while at the same time, Patrick Ewing and the Knicks had only the Bulls and Pacers competing with them for spots in the NBA Finals yearly.

Ewing would score 65 combined over the next two meetings in April 1993 before scoring 30 again on Opening Night that October in a three-point win in Boston. He routinely owned the Celtics during this time, reaching a crescendo with a 36-14 effort in March 1994.

As the Celtics got worse, the Knicks took advantage of them more and more. A 35-point blowout in February 1994 still stands as one of the biggest blowouts in the rivalry's history. Hubert Davis nailed five threes and scored 25 points in a 90-83 win the following month.

It was always a different enemy that flummoxed the Celtics. Charles Smith scoring 25, Anthony Mason scoring 21, and John Starks and Ewing's consistency. Even as Pat Riley turned into Jeff Van Gundy, the Knicks never lost a step.

The streak had reached 17 by January 28, 1997, when the pitiful 9-30 Celtics put the greatest scare into the contending Knicks yet. An eight-point lead in the final minutes dwindled to a tie on a Todd Day three in the final minute before free throws by Antoine Walker gave Boston the lead in the final minute.

Just when the streak appeared over, Chris Childs called game with eight seconds left.

Eventually, the streak would finally end on January 26, 1998, when the Knicks were held to just 85 points behind a 25-point gem by Chauncey Billups. Even this triumphant victory came with an asterisk, as Ewing missed the game due to wrist surgery. Huh.

The Knicks own the Cavs in the playoffs, but did you know there was a stretch they owned them like this?

In five all-time playoff meetings, the Knicks are 16-2 against the Cavs, but once took things to another level in the early 1980s.

Unlike the Celtics, this is pretty peculiar. The Knicks were an average team during this streak, but took advantage of one of the worst eras of Cavs basketball under Ted Stepien.

Quite precisely, this streak can be known as the "Stepien Streak", as while he was owner from April 1980 to his sale in April 1983, the Cavs went 1-16 against the Knicks, with the lone win coming just two weeks before he sold the team in late March of 1983.

Highlights of the streak include Mike Glenn's 29-point game in November 1980 (second-highest scoring game of his career), Ray Williams' 37-point gem in an overtime win two weeks later, and perennially playing in front of 4,000 fans at an empty Richfield Coliseum. The NBA was totally different in the 80s.

Back in the day, there weren't many teams. As such, you get stuff like this.

Over a span of 400 days from February 6, 1952, to March 11, 1953, the Knicks played the Baltimore Bullets 17 times and won every single one of them.

The 1950s Knicks can sometimes be referred to as the Silver Era of Knicks basketball due to the team making multiple Finals appearances before Russell came and made the East his own, so it's no surprise they were dominant. But like this?

The lore of 1950s NBA is quite fascinating. These teams played each other three times in six days in February 1952 when the streak began, but played the games in three different places. The Bullets won 82-81 in the Baltimore Coliseum on February 4, the Knicks won 73-70 at the 69th Regiment Armory on February 6, and the two teams met in Philadelphia on February 8 in a 20-point blowout win for Ray Lumpp and the Knicks.

On March 5, the teams participated in a doubleheader at the Boston Garden, preceding a game between the Bucks and Celtics later that night.

In 1952-53, when the Knicks went 10-0 against the Bullets en route to a Finals appearance, they played one game in Philly, two games in Boston (one of which went to triple overtime), and even played in Trenton, New Jersey, on March 5, 1953.

Finally, the Bullets snapped the skid on November 14, 1953, behind 19 points by Max Zaslofsky in Baltimore.

Just for the hell of it, here's some other weird neutral site locations from the 1950s:

January 29, 1952, in Louisville (vs. Indianapolis Olympians)

February 3, 1953, in Buffalo (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)

February 18, 1953, in Providence (vs. Boston Celtics)

January 22, 1954, in New Haven, CT (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)

Several times in 1954-55 in Miami (vs. Fort Wayne Pistons)

November 18, 1954, in Syracuse (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)

March 3, 1955, in Saratoga Springs (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)

March 13, 1956, in Moorhead, MN (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)

January 17, 1957, in Lacrosse, WI (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)

January 14, 1958, in St. Louis (vs. Cincinnati Royals)

February 21, 1958, in Camden, NJ (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)

January 22, 1962, in Moline, IL (vs. Chicago Packers)

March 12, 1962, in Seattle (vs. Los Angeles Lakers)

Various times in Hershey, PA (including the Wilt 100 game)

We've seen a new standard of excellence for the Knicks since the turn of the decade, They have three of these streaks in the last six years!

Back when the Pistons weren't the annoying playoff contenders we know them as now, they were pretty damn awful. For years, it was a running joke that the COVID-19 pandemic was younger than the last Pistons win over the Knicks.

The streak began on February 8, 2020, when the Knicks overcame an early double-digit deficit to outlast the Pistons in Detroit in a battle of two lowly teams that wouldn't even be invited to the bubble. Another win on March 8 would mark the team's final home game with fans for another year due to the pandemic.

As the Knicks ascended, the Pistons stayed bad. On April 4, 2021, the Knicks eviscerated them by a 125-81 margin, the second-biggest blowout in the over 430 games in this matchup.

Even as the meltdown in 2021-22 ensued, the orange and blue survived a scare that March when Marvin Bagley III dropped 27, only for Alec Burks to strip Cade Cunningham in the final seconds to hold on.

The most memorable game of the streak came at the end. Facing the 8-48 Pistons at home in late February, the Knicks came out sleepy and watched as Cunningham nearly dragged his hapless team to the finish line to end the skid at 14, but shenanigans ensued with Donte DiVincenzo to somehow pull it off with a Josh Hart and-1.

The streak ended on December 7, 2024. We didn't know it at the time, but the Pistons had finally emerged as threats, and they'd start their own six-game regular-season winning streak against the Knicks that lasted until three weeks ago.

The last time the Raptors beat the Knicks? January 22, 2023.

The last time the Nets beat the Knicks? January 28, 2023.

The next opportunity for both to beat the Knicks? Brooklyn gets another chance on December 27, while Toronto next gets a crack on January 20. It'll be basically four years for both since their last win.

These two streaks are tied for the fourth-longest active streaks in the NBA.

The three longer? OKC over Memphis, Cleveland over Washington, and the Clippers over the Hornets, all at 17. If you thought four years was a lot, it's been almost 10 since the Hornets beat the Clippers!

These two streaks are very different, but also the same. Both teams have been worse than the Knicks this entire time, sometimes considerably worse, and have yielded some ugly blowouts.

There have also been plenty of scares. There's the Brunson game-winner in the NBA Cup, the KAT heroics in The Six, the times that Brooklyn puts up a fight but folds late at Barclays Center, and the multiple double-digit comebacks we saw this week.

Either way, that's two Atlantic Division rivals that can't beat the Knicks. It also comes directly after both dominated the Knicks for prolonged periods.

Remember Nic Claxton's comments? Well, at the time, the Nets were 0-9 against the Nets from 2020-23.

The Raptors went a blistering 23-5 against the Knicks from January 2016 to November 2023.

Ain't no fun when the rabbit's got the gun.

#2667. Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflips after Aidan Hutchinson injury

Giants running back Cam Skattebo’s penchant for backflips became a talking point during his recovery from last season’s ankle injury, but he resumed doing them after touchdowns upon his return to action this fall.

#2660. Fernando Mendoza’s painful NFL debut could hold answers to next test vs Broncos

The best thing Fernando Mendoza has going for him Sunday in Denver might be the same thing the Broncos have going for them. Both sides got a good look at what happened to the Raiders rookie against Seattle.

Presumably, both sides hit the rewind button.

Fernando Mendoza (15) of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up before a game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

For Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, the attraction is obvious. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times in his first NFL start. Any coach with a rested pass rush and a home crowd willing to make life miserable for a visiting quarterback would be interested in how they went about it.

For Mendoza, the part worth rewinding might come a second or two before he hit the ground. What did he see when he came to the line? What changed when he got the ball? And where could he have gone with it once it did?

The Broncos present some big-time challenges in that regard.

"It's one of the top defenses in the league for a reason," Mendoza said. "So they are very good, they're very sound and I respect them a lot."

Coach Klint Kubiak is confident the rookie will process and adapt accordingly.

"His approach has been excellent since he got here," Kubiak said. "He's a competitor. It's his first NFL start. I thought he played well enough for us to win, especially in that first half, and we didn't close it out in the second half."

A week ago, those were questions he had to answer against Mike Macdonald's defense without the benefit of a single NFL start. On Sunday, there's at least a chance Joseph asks him something he's heard before.

Consider what Denver can take from the way Seattle made Mendoza account for pressure. A linebacker walking up to the line gives the quarterback something to think about. Put one in each gap alongside the center and now the quarterback and his protection have some decisions to make.

Michael Mayer of the Las Vegas Raiders avoids a tackle from Josh Jobe of the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

The beauty of it for Denver is that neither linebacker has to come. If Mendoza hurries a throw over the middle to beat a blitz and finds a linebacker dropping into the very window he picked out, Joseph will have gotten what he wanted without sending anybody extra.

So where's the opportunity for Mendoza? Start with what happens if that linebacker comes.

Somebody just vacated a valuable piece of real estate. A receiver breaking inside behind him can give Mendoza a throw he can make with his feet set, before the rush has much say in the matter. Six or 7 yards on first down would do wonders for an offense that spent too much of Sunday trying to figure out third-and-long.

There's a bigger throw available, too, if Denver decides to crowd the line and leave a cornerback outside with no safety behind him. That's a chance to give Tre Tucker a ball down the sideline. The trick is confirming the safety really did come down. Seattle gave Mendoza firsthand experience with how much a picture can change between the time a quarterback calls for the ball and the time it reaches his hands.

Getting Tucker involved would go a long way, especially if Brock Bowers' ankle injury keeps him on the sideline. Tucker's ability to stretch the field, and Mendoza's willingness to take some chances on those long throws, could help open things up for the run game and the short and intermediate passing game.

Tyler Linderbaum, left, Fernando Mendoza, center, and Jalen Nailor celebrate a touchdown in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

"There are a lot of variables and what our coach always emphasizes making sure we're taking the positive gain," Mendoza said. "However, those deep shots and those explosives are what can help us win the game. And so, I mean, it's really play-by-play, and I look forward to taking a look at the shots we have this weekend."

Lost in those six sacks is a reason to believe Mendoza can make some of those throws. He completed 11 of 13 passes in the first half against Seattle and got the ball to eight receivers. He already knows what it feels like to take what an NFL defense gives him and move on to the next play.

Kubiak can help him get back to that. Give Mendoza an early throw on a moving pocket. Change where Denver's edge rushers expect to find him. And if the Broncos are getting upfield in a hurry, a well-timed screen gives those rushers an invitation to keep right on going.

Some of which requires a seamless process well ahead of the snap.

"I was very pleased with him getting out of the huddle, him making the correct checks, the correct calls," Kubiak said. "That's what he has shown in practice, his ability to do that and to be able to run the show that way. There's room for growth, but in his first start, I thought that he operated the game like he does in practice."

Of course, there's a limit to what anybody can draw up if the Raiders run for 65 yards on 24 carries again. Joseph had a bye week to study the Raiders. He hardly needed all of it to see the advantage in making Mendoza throw on downs when everyone in the stadium knows he has to.

Denver figures to make the rookie prove he can solve some of the problems Seattle put on tape. Fair enough.

But if the Broncos want to borrow from the Seahawks, Mendoza gets something out of the deal, too. Somewhere in all that film of what went wrong is a throw he'd love to have back.

"The most important thing is how he's playing the game. We'll coach up everything," Kubiak said. "But like I said, and like I told Fernando, I was pleased because of the preparation that he put in. The things that he did in practice showed up in the game, and he's going to have a lot of things to learn and grow from."

#2658. JJ Redick revealed the Lakers’ strategy with two-way signings this season

Tuesday night, with Walker Kessler sidelined and his replacement, Kevon Looney, struggling, the Los Angeles Lakers turned to Carson Cooper for minutes at center. Signed to a two-way contract on Nov. 10, Cooper gave the Lakers 18 minutes and logged three points (0-of-1 shooting, 3-of-6 at the line), four rebounds (two offensive) and two assists. Los Angeles outscored the Charlotte Hornets by six points during his time on the floor.

After Cooper's Lakers debut, head coach JJ Redick spoke about what the organization is prioritizing with its two-way contract players, whether it's Cooper, Chris Mañon, Arthur Kaluma or AK Okereke (who was waived last month and is now playing for the Coachella Valley Lakers).

The goal, Redick said, isn't to simply land the foremost G League stars but to find those who can fill valuable roles for the Lakers when called upon, just as Cooper did Tuesday.

"I think [Carson Cooper] understands the assignment. Not to get too big picture with what the G League is and what the two-ways are, but I think philosophically, we've gone in a bunch of different directions with our two-ways and I think with this group, like we really wanted to get guys that could play a role for this team if needed," Redick told reporters following the 118-114 win. "With Chris and with both the AKs…and Carson's the same way. He's here to play a role and it's not, 'Oh, this guy can go score 30 points in the G League.' That doesn't necessarily equate to what we need right now. And so all our guys that are two-ways this year, they understand why they're in that role and how they can impact winning and help our team and he did that tonight for us."

Kessler isn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so the Lakers will welcome back their preferred choice at center against the Utah Jazz. But given Looney's struggles to open the year and the general lack of reliable options behind Kessler, it's absolutely possible Cooper receives some more run down the line this season. At the very least, it sounds like Tuesday was a nice audition in his head coach's eyes.

New Orleans needs a change. Sunday's loss was another reminder that this current regime just isn't getting the job done. The Saints cannot keep wasting opportunities in a division that remains wide open.

It's time for the Saints to stop pretending things are going to get better without making a change.

#2653. Giants’ Cam Skattebo makes abrupt backflip declaration: ‘I’m serious’

Giants star running back Cam Skattebo insisted Wednesday that he would no longer perform his signature backflip celebration during games.

His decision came in the wake of Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tearing his ACL while doing a simple leaping sack celebration on Sunday.

During Thursday night's loss to the Commanders, three Giants players — Skattebo and wide receivers Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney — all did backflips in the end zone after Skattebo scored a touchdown.

Fields said Wednesday that Giants coach John Harbaugh did not address the team about Hutchinson's injury. So Harbaugh didn't tell Skattebo or anybody else to avoid a backflip celebration in the future.

Skattebo reached the decision on his own.

"I'm done flipping, just for that reason," Skattebo said of Hutchinson's injury. "It's hard to see. Don't want it to happen to me."

"I'm serious," he said when pressed. "There's no reason to flip. Mentally, I'm like: 'F--- it. I'm not doing that s---.'"

He added, regarding Hutchinson's injury, "That s--- ain't going to happen to me."

Skattebo meant he would avoid that sort of unforced season-ending injury by no longer doing his backflip celebration.

Still, at one point during a brief interview on Wednesday, Skattebo left the door slightly ajar to his back flip returning.

"I'm sure I'll do it at some point, if we go to the playoffs or something," he said.

Before Skattebo granted an interview on the matter, he chimed in while Fields was discussing Hutchinson's injury.

"Just bad luck, man," Skattebo said from his nearby locker. "Just bad luck."

Skattebo suffered a gruesome season-ending ankle injury last year, but that didn't happen during a backflip situation.

This past offseason, at a fan event in Manhattan, Skattebo took a spill while attempting a backflip on a stage. He was not injured.

After that incident, Harbaugh essentially told Skattebo to stop doing backflips in off-field or non-game situations.

Skattebo said during training camp that he would avoid doing backflips in any non-game settings, including practices. He was noncommittal about whether the touchdown celebration would return during games in 2026. It has.

#2648. Maikel Garcia-Bryce Miller trade gives fantasy rebound candidates new life

Reports emerged Tuesday that the Royals were considering trading Maikel Garcia for pitching help. The Mariners made those reports outdated quickly by meeting those demands.

Per ESPN's Jeff Passan, Seattle acquired Garcia on Wednesday along with relief pitchers James McArthur and L.P. Langevin in exchange for starting pitcher Bryce Miller, plus additional arms Logan Evans and Jose Ferrer.

The change of scenery spices up a pivotal 2027 for both headliners. Does this make either Garcia or Miller a better fantasy baseball pick for 2027 (assuming we have a season)?

MLB Free Agent Tracker 2026-27: Top players available, latest signings, and contract information

Stay up to date with the MLB free agent market this offseason, including player signings, contract details, and more as the 2026-27 Hot Stove gets underway.

After a breakout 2025 season (.286/.351/.449, 16 HR, 23 steals, 81 runs, 74 RBI) in which he received AL MVP votes, Garcia endured several stints on the sidelines.

A hand muscle strain that cost him more than a month during the summer, and he had other shorter bouts with elbow cramps, an early-season right hamstring strain, and a late-summer left hamstring strain.

That would explain his crater-like drop in stolen bases to just five in 2026. When you invest in Garcia, you want that security with stolen bases and batting-average base.

Sure, that statistic as a whole is volatile, but as Garcia's Baseball Savant/Statcast chart spells out, his combination of elite Chase/Whiff/Strikeout percentages point to one of the batters likeliest to have the fewest strikeouts in the majors.

In addition, his top-level glove work would keep him in the lineup so he could eventually fall upward toward 20 homers, just like what happened in 2025.

This may prove difficult, though. Garcia already sits near the bottom of annual lists in barrel rate, which doesn't predict heavy power growth without supremely good luck or a rapid bulk-up from his 6-foot-1, 195-pound frame.

Moving to T-Mobile Park, the Park Factor for right-handed hitters overall, for doubles, and for triples sits toward the bottom of the 29-park rankings, if not the bottom; homer ratings remained almost the same.

Much of Garcia's ability to regain his fantasy juice sits on how quickly he'll return to elite steal totals. Heading into his age-27 season, Garcia carries 2,174 plate appearances, more than what's typically needed before a significant breakthrough happens.

Plus, nestled in the middle of the Mariners order likely will serve him better than helping to carry a cooked Kansas City order that wilted aside from Bobby Witt.

His rebound potential and improved supporting cast likely will justify a return to the top-100 overall picks in fantasy drafts, with a significant positional advantage of a stolen-base upside play at third base.

Miller is still trying to round back into his peak form following a 2025 marred with bone spurs and inflammation in his right (throwing) elbow that helped lead to a 5.68 ERA, a far cry from 2.94 in his breakout 2024.

Despite missing time with an oblique strain, Miller looked like he was turning a corner in the first half last season; he held a 2.18 ERA at the All-Star break.

He took an ugly turn in the second half, though, dragging himself to a 6.05 ERA and a temporary move to the bullpen. Perhaps endurance was a challenge following his elbow concerns the year before.

Settling in at season's end with a palatable 4.18 ERA, many year-over-year improvements stand out, including:

Swinging Strike%: 10.6 to career-best 11.6

Perhaps a contributor to his first-half success was an offseason treatment that proved successful without surgery, according to MLB.com's Daniel Kramer's report from February:

"But the Mariners right-hander discovered a solution early in the offseason that allowed him to avoid undergoing a procedure that he'd long envisioned as inevitable.

The answer was a Synvisc injection, gleaned from consultations with renowned orthopedist Dr. Keith Meister and applied to improve joint lubrication, dampen inflammation -- and above all, relieve pain.

"After I got that, that's when I started feeling a lot better," Miller said. "I thought for sure I was going to have to get the spurs shaved down and removed."

Perhaps better management of the spurs will lead to more sustained results -- meaning Miller could once again deliver as an often fantasy ace throughout the season.

Jose A. Ferrer (4.18 ERA, 3 saves, 13 holds last year) should remain on watch lists for saves and holds leagues.

Logan Evans might eventually compete for a rotation spot with the Royals, but his middling stuff should limit fantasy interest to spot starts and AL-only leagues.

#2643. Austin Reaves remains out vs. Jazz, Walker Kessler returns

Following a dramatic overtime win against the Hornets on Tuesday, the Lakers will still be at nearly full strength against the Jazz on the second night of a back-to-back, with one major exception.

Austin Reaves will miss his third game since suffering a heel bruise against the Bucks last Wednesday. However, he is the only player on the injury report for the purple and gold with Walker Kessler, who also missed Tuesday's game, set to return.

There are multiple players notable in their exclusion from this injury report. First, as noted, Kessler will return after being out with leg soreness on Tuesday.

"Walker, some lower leg soreness, got bumped," head coach JJ Redick said before Tuesday's game. "Just thinking big picture. We don't think it's serious, but it makes sense for him to, as a precautionary, be out tonight."

Luka Dončić playing both legs of the back-to-back is notable, too. Luka's two missed games this season have both been during a back-to-back, but he did play in the team's previous back-to-back at home.

As for Austin, Redick said Tuesday that he would do on-court work Wednesday morning to see where he's at. The injury and return remain a pain tolerance matter with Redick having previously said that there is no structural damage with the injury.

It is easier to be patient with Reaves' return with the Lakers winning. But with a match-up with the Spurs looming, it would also be nice to see him return soon so he can take part in that contest.

As for the Jazz, who are also on the second night of a back-to-back, their injury report is nearly the same as it was against the Clippers. Jaxson Hayes, who was out on Tuesday, has been upgraded to questionable.

Jaren Jackson, Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkic are all out. Kobe Bufkin also will not be making his return to LA as he is with Utah's two-way team.

#2642. Vic Fangio sends vote of confidence to Cowboys’ Christian Parker after losing playcalling

Vic Fangio sends vote of confidence to Cowboys' Christian Parker after losing playcalling appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker may have lost his playcalling duties, but not the confidence of at least one fellow defensive coordinator in him.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Philadelphia Eagles DC Vic Fangio shared his thoughts on Parker, who will not be calling plays for the Cowboys defense after losing the duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.

The 68-year-old Fangio even cited examples to support his belief that everything will be just fine for Parker, who is in only his first year as a defensive coordinator in the NFL.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Well, patience is not in overabundance in today's society, especially in the sports world," Fangio said, via a video shared by Eagles reporter Eliot Shorr-Parks of 94WIP.

"But, Christian will recover from that. You know, it happened to Sean Payton many years ago in New York. But I think he's recovered nicely. You know, Joe Brady, who's the head coach of Buffalo, he got fired during the season, then he kept on. I think he's recovered nicely. Mike LaFleur in Arizona, the Jets fired him during the season a couple of years ago. He's recovered nicely. Christian will do the same thing. He'll be fine."

Fangio also has some familiarity with Parker, and vice versa. Before he was hired by the Cowboys, Parker was with the Eagles from 2024 to 2025, serving in the roles of passing game coordinator & defensive backs coach.

The latest development in Parker's role in managing the Cowboys' defense came on the heels of Dallas' 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in a Week 10 game at AT&T Stadium in Arlington last Sunday, in which Christian McCaffrey and company went off for 584 total yards.

#2641. Marlon Humphrey apologizes for saying Baltimore is "best at making criminals"

Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey found himself in some hot water for comments he made about Baltimore on Wednesday.

During a since-deleted episode of his podcast, Humphrey said “they’re best at making criminals” when asked what the city is best at making. Humphrey’s words were met with an angry response in the city and he tried to walk them back with an apology while speaking to reporters after practice.

“As you guys know, I’ve been here my whole career,” Humphrey said, via Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com. “Spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I’m an investor in the city, an investor in different areas (and) parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and just would like to apologize for those comments.”

Humphrey’s apology was noted by Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott, who wondered in a social media post how Humphrey would respond “if prominent Baltimoreans used their platform to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way.” Scott added that “a verbal apology is not enough” for those who look up to Ravens players and invited Humphrey to meet with people in the city working on “preventing others from making the mistakes they made.”

#2639. Commanders, Cowboys get help from schedule in effort to chase down the Giants

The New York Giants are leading the NFC East after 10 weeks of play, but the gap is closing. The Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are hoping to take them down.

There likely will only be one team coming out of the division for the playoffs, and the Giants want to make sure they are the ones that come out on top. Here's a look at each team's remaining schedule and how difficult it will be for each team to navigate.

Current standing: 4–6, second place in NFC East

Remaining opponents: Titans, Eagles, at Seahawks, at Rams, Jaguars, Giants, at Commanders

The Cowboys have one of the easier remaining schedules in the league, but they remain in second place in the division behind the Giants. They have very winnable games coming up, with the Titans and Eagles on deck, but then things get more difficult with the Seahawks, Rams, and Jaguars before the rematch against the Giants at AT&T Stadium later in the season.

That three-game stretch before that rematch against the Giants could knock them out. Some wins against some powerful teams will likely keep them in the hunt and give them some momentum before facing the Giants in their first game of the 2027 calendar year.

Current standing: 3-5-1, third place in NFC East

Remaining opponents: Bengals, at Cardinals, at Titans, Texans, Falcons, at Vikings, at Jaguars, Cowboys

The Commanders' win against the Giants on Thursday Night Football last week kept their season alive, and their schedule is about to get easier.

After this week's Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, the schedule gets much easier for the Commanders. They will play four consecutive games against teams that don't have a better record than them, which could lead into a run leading up to the end of the season.

The final three games are a bit more challenging, as they face two likely playoff teams on the road before finishing the season against the Cowboys in a game that could decide the division if the Giants fold in the second half of the year.

Remaining opponents: Jaguars, at Colts, 49ers, at Seahawks, Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, Eagles

The Giants have one of the toughest schedules remaining in the league, as only three teams will face a more challenging gauntlet in the second half of the season. With seven games to go, four come against teams that are likely heading to the playoffs.

If they were to lose all four of those games, they would need to sweep the Colts, Cowboys, and Eagles in order to get to eight wins. That might be enough to win the NFC East this year, but it is far from a guarantee.

The Giants should want to beat some of these top teams to give them reason to believe that they can compete in the playoffs. That all starts with this weekend's contest against the Jaguars, which is arguably the team's toughest test to date.

Kickoff between the Jags and Giants is scheduled for Sunday at 4:25 p.m. inside MetLife Stadium. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount+ app.

#2637. Media firebrand asks if Black players will let Lakers’ ‘white brothers’ win it all

Stephen A. Smith had a question for Black NBA players on Wednesday morning after the Lakers won their ninth straight game.

"These white brothers can play, they can play. They can win a championship. This is the NBA!" Smith said on "First Take." "Y'all gonna let them win a championship?"

Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams, Luka Doncic, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler wait during a time-out in Phoenix, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Darryl Webb

Smith was talking about a Lakers team built around Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler.

A week earlier, he had picked Los Angeles to bow out by the second round, saying on Mad Dog Sports Radio that he had never seen a team win a title with three white players as its best players.

He still doubts the Lakers will win it all, but he and fellow ESPN analyst Chiney Ogwumike agree they can.

Smith framed the question around race. Ogwumike made the stronger case for the Lakers by pointing to what Doncic did with the game on the line. He trusted Quentin Grimes to take the biggest shot of the night.

Luka Doncic reacts to making a bad pass during the second half against the Charlotte Hornets in Los Angeles, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Getty Images

But Smith made the question about race. Ogwumike pointed to something that says more about the Lakers' title chances. With the game on the line, Luka Doncic trusted Quentin Grimes to take the biggest shot of the night.

The final possession of regulation in Tuesday's 118-114 overtime win over Charlotte gave her a reason to believe. With Reaves and Kessler sidelined, the Lakers had rallied from 18 down and needed a 3 to stay alive. Doncic had 36 points and a single defender in front of him. Grimes had his hands up.

Quentin Grimes of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after scoring during a game against the Charlotte Hornets in Los Angeles, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Getty Images

Doncic found him. Grimes buried the tying 3 with 1.7 seconds left. It was his 10th of the night, making him and Kobe Bryant the only Lakers to hit that many in a game. Grimes finished with a career-high 47.

"It's the vibe. It's the ability to say, 'Hey, we have enough to pursue a championship,'" Ogwumike said on ESPN. "Not gonna lie, when I heard that, I was like, I'm not sure about that."

Where Smith raised the question of race, Ogwumike saw what could make the Lakers champions: chemistry developing between the Lakers' best player and a new addition attempting to make his mark.

"That doesn't start in that moment," she said. "That starts in training camp."

#2629. How LeBron James' move from Lakers to 76ers unlocked both teams' superpowers

The NBA standings, heading into games scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 18, tell a remarkable story involving LeBron James.

The Los Angeles Lakers, the team James left before the 2026-27 season, are 13-2 and off to their best start since 2008-09 (14-1 to start that season). That season, the Lakers won the NBA title.

The Philadelphia 76ers, the team James joined before this season, are 12-3 and off to their best start since 2000-01. That season, the 76ers reached the NBA Finals and lost to…the Lakers.

"You never know what… change can totally affect your team,'' said Randy Pfund, part of the Lakers coaching staff from 1985 to 1994 and general manager of the Miami Heat from 1995 to 2008.

Of course the oddity here is, four weeks into the season, the team James left and the team he joined both appear to have gotten better.

Analytics can help explain how the Lakers are thriving without James. Especially as presented by Vangelis Sarlis, a Greek postdoctoral researcher who has mined NBA data.

"I would describe it as role redistribution rather than addition by subtraction,'' Vangelis Sarlis told USA TODAY Sports. "…The more persuasive analytical explanation is that LeBron's departure clarified roles.''

With James no longer playing for the Lakers, Luka Dončić leads the league in scoring with 38.8 points per game and twice has scored more than 50 points.

"Luka Dončić is now the unquestioned primary creator and Austin Reaves the secondary creator, with personnel around them designed for spacing, screening and finishing,'' said Sarlis, whose research team includes George Papageorgiou and professor Christos Tjortjis at International Hellenic University in Thermi, Greece.

Their work includes the 2024 academic paper titled "Leveraging Sports Analytics and Association Rule Mining to Uncover Recovery and Economic Impacts in NBA Basketball."

Through 14 games, Sarlis pointed out that the Lakers' offensive rating had risen from 118.2 last season to about 123 points per 100 possessions, the best in the league. He also cited NBA tracking that shows the Lakers have experienced the league's biggest jump in transition scoring, from 22.6 to 26.2 points per game.

"That supports the observation that the offense looks quicker and more fluid,'' Sarlis said. He also noted Dončić's usage rate of 40.2%, which leads the league in adding to the Lakers' offense: "It's faster, but it is more concentrated, not less.''

Then there was James' $52 million salary with the Lakers.

The funds once spent on him allowed the Lakers to re-sign Reeves and overhaul the roster. Key additions include center Walker Kessler, who's averaging 14.5 points per game and 10.9 rebounds per game; guard Quentin Grimes, who is averaging 12.1 points per game and scored 47 points in the Lakers' 118-114 overtime victory against the Charlotte Hornets Tuesday, Nov. 17; and Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Sexton, both notable contributors.

"That personnel is…the most concrete link to LeBron's departure,'' Sarlis said.

LeBron James is not the same player who won four NBA titles, including one with the Lakers during the COVID-shortened season in 2020.

In 11 games played this season, James' shooting percentage (.443) is the worst since his rookie year and his 3-point shooting percentage (.225) is the worst of his career. But Bob Whitsitt, former general manager of the Seattle Supersonics and Portland Trail Blazers, suggested the early-season shooting trouble obscures James' contributions.

"He's always been a good passer, but maybe right now his passing is a little bit more of what's needed in Philly than the other things he's doing,'' Whitsitt said.

James leads the 76ers with 6.9 assists per game. No one seems to be overly concerned he's averaging only 15.1 points on a team with potent scorers like Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid.

"Rather than expecting LeBron to remain the primary scorer, the 76ers can utilize him as a fourth scoring option, playmaker and facilitator alongside Embiid, Maxey, and Brown,'' said Sarlis, the Greek researcher. "His experience and basketball intelligence could help optimize team rotations and strengthen Philadelphia's pursuit of another championship.''

Pfund won two NBA championship rings as a member of the Lakers' coaching staff from 1985 to 1994. He won a third NBA championship ring as the general manager of the Miami Heat from 1995 to 2008.

He also spent most of his NBA career working for legendary Pat Riley.

"Pat always believed you could never have too many veteran guys who would come through in the clutch,'' Pfund said.

Sarlis said his team's research shows James, 41, is among the most consistent historical performers in decisive moment.

Clutch veterans are most valuable in the playoffs, said Pfund, who cited two examples.

In February 1987, when Pfund was an assistant on the Lakers' coaching staff, Lakers traded for center Mychal Thompson. He was was an 8th-year NBA veteran. Not only did he prove to be a capable backup center behind Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, he also played a role in the Lakers' winning the 1987 NBA title.

Then in 2005, when Pfund was the general manager of the Heat, the team at Riley's behest traded for Antoine Walker. He was an 11th year veteran and three-time All Star with the Boston Celtics.

"He was pretty average all year,'' Pfund said. "And people were (saying), man, they spent too much money and whatever.''

But the veteran player delivered in the postseason., according Pfund.

"Antoine Walker had made a lot of big baskets,'' Pfund said. "He didn't hesitate at all.''

The Heat beat the Dallas Mavericks in the 2006 NBA title, winning the franchise's first NBA title.

It's still five weeks away from the NBA's slate of Christmas Day games, which this year will include -- you guessed it -- the 76ers vs. the Lakers at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

But Whitsitt, the former NBA general manager, allowed himself to think well beyond Christmas.

"What kind of story would it be if the Lakers played the Sixers in the Finals?'' he said.

It's an enticing possibility as Whitsitt talked about what he expects to happen next. James will continue to blend in with his new teammates. The Lakers will eventually tighten up on defense. Hopefully, both teams will stay healthy as the season unfolds.

"They're both fun to watch,'' Whitsitt said.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: How LeBron James' move from Lakers to 76ers unlocked both teams' superpowers

#2627. Panthers could get 3 players back from injured reserve this week, including CB Mike Jackson

CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are slowly getting healthier following a rash of injuries in the first half of the season.

Panthers coach Dave Canales said cornerback Mike Jackson, running back Jonathon Brooks and offensive lineman Brady Christensen were full participants in practice Wednesday and proclaimed them "ready" to return from injured reserve in time for Sunday's home game against the Baltimore Ravens.

All three players remain in the 21-day practice window, so the Panthers would first need to make room for them on the 53-man roster.

"These guys are hungry to get back out there, so we are going to try to find a way for them to help us," Canales said.

Cornerback Will Lee III is also set to return this week from a nagging hamstring injury.

Canales also remains optimistic that two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaycee Horn and starting left tackle Ickey Ekwonu will return at some point this season, although he hasn't given a precise timetable.

The news comes one week after outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips returned from a three-game absence because of a hamstring injury to earn NFC Defensive Player of the Week following Carolina's 20-17 win over New Orleans.

Also, wide receiver Xavier Legette returned from IR last week, although he played sparingly.

All of that is good news for a Panthers (4-5) team that is clinging to first place in the NFC South despite their losing record.

"We have a lot of special guys ... that have done a lot of work trying to come back, and this is an opportunity to rally with our teammates," quarterback Bryce Young said.

The return of Jackson could be a tremendous lift for the Panthers as they prepare to face Baltimore wide receiver Zay Flowers.

Jackson led the NFL in pass breakups last season with 19 and would give Carolina's cornerback room some needed experience.

Jackson and Horn have been out since Week 4, and backups Lee and Akayleb Evans went down with injuries in the weeks that followed. That forced the Panthers into playing their fifth and sixth cornerbacks the past few weeks, resulting in several pass interference and defensive holding penalties.

Canales said it's "going to be awesome" to get Jackson back on the field.

"With Mike out there, there is the leadership complement," Canales said. "He's a guy that we have been counting on this whole time. And he's excited. He sees people making plays and he wants to be out there making plays."

Brooks would be a welcome addition to the Panthers backfield.

Carolina has been relying almost exclusively on Chuba Hubbard to carry the load in the running game. He ran 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints and also caught five passes for 80 yards.

He has at least 19 carries in five of Carolina's past seven games.

The Panthers haven't given many carries to Trevor Etienne or A.J. Dillon to help spell Hubbard. However, Canales has always been high on Brooks, whom he views as a "home run threat" on any given play.

Canales will have to keep an eye on new injuries to tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble this week. Both sat out practice Wednesday with knee injuries, and Canales said the team won't know much on their status until later in the week.

#2626. The missing Gen-Z reaction that told JJ Redick this Lakers team was special

Long before the Lakers were the best story in the NBA, JJ Redick had an inkling that this team was different.

It clicked for him after the Lakers had a team dinner at Carbone Riviera in Las Vegas in July.

After general manager Rob Pelinka paid the bill, Redick became hyperaware of what had not happened that evening.

"I get up to leave and, it struck me, nobody had left," Redick said. "Nobody had been on their phone."

But they were indicative of the character of the group. The players wanted to bond. They wanted to be around one another.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic reacts to a charging foul during a game against the Charlotte Hornets, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images

They were in Sin City, surrounded by a million distractions, but they chose to spend their time with one another.

Now a team that was expected to be a mile behind the Thunder and Spurs in the Western Conference has the best record in the league at 13-2. They've won nine games in a row. They've announced themselves as real championship contenders.

The Lakers have surpassed expectations. They're leading the league in offensive rating (123.1) and steals (10.8), and they are third in blocks (6.1).

Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick calls out directions against the Portland Trail Blazers in Los Angeles on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. Getty Images

Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves constantly tease each other as though they were brothers. Their affinity for one another has spilled onto the court, where they're the top-scoring duo in the league, averaging a combined 63.5 points per game.

Walker Kessler has a contagious positivity. He's also a beast down low and a double-double machine, averaging 14.5 points and 10.9 rebounds per game.

And the Lakers' role players are starring in their roles.

That was never more obvious than in the Lakers' 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets on Tuesday. The Lakers were without Kessler (right lower leg soreness) and Reaves (left heel bruise). Doncic was in foul trouble. The Lakers trailed by as much as 18 points.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, slaps hands with head coach JJ Redick during an NBA game Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill

Doncic realized Quentin Grimes had a hot hand. He started waving off Redick's play calls in the fourth quarter, so he could feed his teammate. Grimes went on to finish with a career-high 47 points, becoming the only Laker to score 10 or more 3-pointers in a game other than Kobe Bryant in the Lakers' win.

Things have just come together for the Lakers.

There's a good feeling in the locker room. The guys genuinely like each other. And that's dangerous for the rest of the league.

"I think at the end of the day we have great chemistry, which is in my opinion very important," Doncic said. "But I think this group is very special."

It's interesting because the Lakers weren't supposed to jell this quickly.

Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick looks on against the Atlanta Hawks during the fourth quarter at State Farm Arena in Atlanta on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Getty Images

They have nine new players. Doncic has never been known as a vocal leader. This was supposed to be a transition year after LeBron James left in free agency and the Lakers overhauled their roster around the Slovenian superstar.

But something happened over the summer that changed things.

A seed was planted in Vegas. And it flourished after Doncic flew his teammates to Slovenia to host a mini camp, something he had never done before in his career.

They laughed. They sightsaw. They bonded with each other and grew a much deeper understanding of their biggest star.

Redick believes what's happening right now is a magical coalescence of opportunity meeting the right personnel.

It has resulted in a locker room with good vibes. A team that's soaring. And a coach who is deeply grateful that his gut feeling was correct.

He first saw it months ago, long before they ever stepped foot on the court.

"I don't know what this is going to look like after 82 games," Redick said. "I don't know what it's going to look like after 50. But I do know that there's something with this group. Every special group doesn't mean you win a championship.

#2624. Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum hears criticism, but isn’t moved

Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum didn't become a superstar over night, but it was a quicker development than usual. The former Duke Blue Devil dazzled in his rookie season and nearly led the C's to the NBA Finals in 2018 — all before turning 21 years old. From that point on, especially as Boston established itself as a perennial contender, Tatum was put under a microscope.

The media hyper-analyzed his relationship with former Celtics star Jaylen Brown (a practice that continues to this day), attacked him for not being flamboyant enough, and questioned his clutch factor. The criticism persisted even when Tatum helped Boston end a 16-year title drought in 2024, as many online commenters mocked his post-championship celebration, labelling it disingenuous and saying he was copying other NBA greats, including Celtics legend Kevin Garnett and five-time Los Angeles Lakers champion Kobe Bryant. Although the 28-year-old rarely addresses those who ridicule him, he laughed when asked about them during an interview with Boardroom. Tatum then collected himself before providing a thoughtful answer:

"Listen, I'm all for the trolling and the funny memes and videos, especially on social media," he began. "Does it invoke anything in me? No, not at all. I understand the place that I hold in the NBA and oftentimes (that) comes with a lot of praise, and you got to take your fair share of moments where people want to talk (expletive) about you."

For Tatum, achieving his basketball dreams in exchange for online backlash seems like a worthwhile tradeoff. He emphasized that all of the best players in the world are critiqued, regardless of whether the flak is warranted.

"You can't have it just one way," he said. "And I think...that's part of being a superstar. People on the Internet got a lot of time on their hands."

While some stars take it upon themselves to confront trolls on social media, Tatum has always preferred to settle things on the court. Perhaps this spurning of often faceless detractors is why he draws so much ire online, but also why he commands the respect of basketball's biggest names, including the likes of LeBron James, Kevin Durant, Chris Paul, and others.

"(Expletive) it, we won," Tatum said in response to those claiming his joy after winning it all was performative. "I don't care what y'all say."

To put it simply, Tatum is more than an NBA champion and a six-time All-Star. He's a father who prioritizes his children over engaging with manufactured drama.

His reaction to Brown calling him a liar on Instagram — which has been one of the biggest media controversies of the early season — confirms that.

"I understand (it) being the entertainment business," Tatum told reporters in late October. "Personally, I'm not much of an off-the-court entertainer type of guy...I got two kids."

Listen to "On a Celtics-Mavs blowout, a Magic loss, and a Denver Nuggets showdown" on Spreaker.

#2623. NBA Europe appears headed for 'soft launch' next fall

Commissioner Adam Silver has said he wants NBA Europe to launch in the fall of 2027 — and it appears he is going to get his wish.

Sort of. Just not in the way he or others may have originally envisioned.

There are only 11 months between now and Silver's proposed launch date, and NBA Europe has yet to have any formal agreements with teams. Negotiations with the EuroLeague — some of the teams the NBA is eyeing are members of it — have slowed. That could lead to a "soft launch" of the league next fall, reports The Athletic's Joe Vardon. A member of one of the ownership groups of a potential NBA Europe club put it this way to Vardon:

"Broadly speaking, it is implausible that a serious league could be launched (by next October)."

The idea of a "soft launch" has been floated before and is not something the NBA has pushed back on — this was always a possibility. Building something sustainable long term was always going to take time and the league understood that.

The NBA is partnering with FIBA (the international basketball organization that puts on the World Cup and helps pick teams for the Olympics) on an NBA Europe plan that calls for 12 permanent teams and four open spots teams could play their way into through domestic leagues and tournaments. Those dozen permanent teams would be made up of some existing European powerhouses — FC Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, and Panathinaikos of Greece have been mentioned, among others — plus teams in major European markets such as Rome, Paris, Lyon and others (some of those teams could be tied to existing soccer powers, but not all).

What would make things smoother is an agreement or merger with the EuroLeague — the continent's existing preeminent basketball competition — but a couple of months ago EuroLeague shareholders rejected the NBA's initial proposal. The challenge is that EuroLeague has 13 permanent members and only some of them would be jumping to NBA Europe, which is a bit messy. That said, the sides are still talking, and it's possible they reach some kind of arrangement.

What would a "soft launch" look like? From The Athletic:

So, a soft launch could, in theory, include a qualifying tournament in the fall of 2027. Another possibility for NBA Europe's 2027 version is if, as expected, the NBA formalizes agreements with at least some existing European teams to join as NBA Europe licensed franchises over the next few months. Those teams could play each other in some precursory competition that ultimately becomes NBA Europe.

NBA owners are fully backing Silver and the NBA Europe plan because it's essentially free money for them. Silver and the NBA have met with potential teams and investors and expect franchise fees in the $500 million to $1 billion range for each of the 12 permanent members.

What the NBA wants is to modernize – and better monetize — the basketball infrastructure in Europe. As part of its plan, the league is looking at a multibillion-dollar infrastructure fund to pay for arena construction, including for existing teams (which may already have arenas), bringing more modern NBA-style arenas to those cities.

#2621. Chargers Week 10 PFF Grades: Del’Shawn Phillips lead spirited effort vs. Ravens rushing attack

The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop.

Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton's 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well.

Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise.

You can't be much more dominant than that.

Let's go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night.

TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8OG Logan Taylor – 74.4QB Justin Herbert – 73.0WR Tre' Harris – 72.0FB Scott Matlock – 70.2

It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night.

Monday was Taylor's best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best.

For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026.

Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high.

During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He's done an excellent job as the team's starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton.

OT Travis Burke – 39.5WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4OG Cole Strange – 53.4WR Derius Davis – 53.6WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1

Unfortunately the team's first win of the year was also one of Burke's worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0.

Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them.

The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt's 53.2.

LB Del'Shawn Phillips – 90.6DT Teair Tart – 82.8CB Donte Jackson – 77.4EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0

What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it's turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team's only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent.

Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well.

Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way.

Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three.

Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team's first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season.

Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2618. Brian Schottenheimer has been unable to conquer this team problem

Penalties seem as old as time with the Dallas Cowboys. From 2020 to 2024, under Mike McCarthy, the Cowboys ranked first in the NFL with 570 penalties. It became a consistent talking point every Sunday with McCarthy at the helm and has continued under Brian Schottenheimer.

Penalties aren't always the defining trait that makes a bad team. The Houston Texans are second with 195 penalties since 2025, and the Denver Broncos are tied for third with 193. The combined record for both of those teams is 36-16. It's the type of penalties the Cowboys have been getting—emblematic of what the last few years under Schottenheimer have felt like.

On defense, it's the holding calls or pass interference calls on a critical third-and-long that keep them on the field and the drive moving for the opposing offense. Dallas is tied with the Green Bay Packers for the NFL lead in automatic first downs (9) given via penalty on third down. The Cowboys also lead all teams with 22 penalties resulting in an automatic first down for opponents.

The most defining penalty of the season—and maybe the culture of the entire organization—came versus the Indianapolis Colts, when DeMarvion Overshown ran out on the field as an inactive player. The Cowboys still led 20-17 at that point, but the 15-yard penalty set them back, and the offense ended up punting back to Indy, who tied the game on the next possession.

Then, late in the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers, George Pickens got a taunting penalty as the offense is trying to score quickly and avoid wasting time off the clock. Instead of being at the 49ers' 19-yard line, they got moved back to the 28. It took another six plays and a precious 42 seconds off the clock.

Again, there are many reasons why the Cowboys sit at a 4-6 record. Penalties aren't the only reason they are on the outside looking in as the playoff race starts to take shape. However, penalties signal an undisciplined team, and being the league leader over the last two seasons is starting to negatively define the culture Schottenheimer is building in Dallas.

The Houston Astros have chosen Brad Ausmus as their next manager, the team announced on Wednesday

Ausmus replaces Joe Espada, whose contract as Houston manager was not renewed after three seasons. Espada led the Astros to the playoffs in two of those seasons.

"I am very excited to be back in Houston," Ausmus said in a statement. "The Astros and the city of Houston have been a huge part of my life, and I'm thrilled to create a new chapter as the team's manager. I'd like to thank [general manager Randy Flores] and the entire Astros organization for this opportunity, and I can't wait to get to work."

Ausmus, 57, had served as bench coach for the New York Yankees since late 2023. Prior to that, he had two stints as a big-league manager. He first managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014-17, and over that span he guided the team to a 314-332 record and a division title in his first season. Ausmus also managed the Angels to a 72-90 record in 2019. Overall, Ausmus as a manager has a winning percentage of .478 in five seasons.

Before his dugout career, Ausmus was a top defensive catcher for years. Ausmus's playing career spanned parts of 18 seasons in Major League Baseball, 10 of which came with the Astros. Along the way, Ausmus won three Gold Gloves behind the mask and earned an All-Star selection as a member of the Tigers in 1999.

"We are thrilled to welcome Brad back to the Astros organization," Flores said in a statement. "Brad impressed us throughout the interview process, demonstrating the leadership, energy, and expertise critical to driving a winning culture both on and off the field. I am excited to work alongside Brad and happy to have him back in an Astros uniform."

With Houston, Ausmus is the first major hire undertaken by Flores, who himself was named to his post earlier in the offseason. The Astros are coming off a division title and a postseason berth in 2026. However, they also finished 81-81 and had a negative run differential. It's an uncertain future, as the Astros have an aging roster in spots, a weak farm system, and multiple core contributors entering their walk years in 2027.

It remains to be seen whether owner Jim Crane will try to wring out another season of contention from the roster or lean into a rebuild. Whatever the course, Ausmus will help guide it in a city where he remains a highly popular figure.

As of Houston's decision to hire Ausmus, the Los Angeles Angels are the only team with a current managerial vacancy. Earlier in the offseason, the Philadelphia Phillies retained interim manager Don Mattingly on a permanent basis, as did the New York Mets with Andy Green, and the Seattle Mariners replaced Dan Wilson with Jason Kanzler.

#2614. Vikings-49ers First Injury Report

The Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers released their first injury reports in advance of their matchup on Sunday night at the Azteca in Mexico City. The 49ers held a walk-through in their temporary location in Colorado, while the Vikings held a regular practice.

PUP = Physically unable to participate list.

IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed.

Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day.

Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day.

Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day.

Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing.

For the Vikings, it looks like just Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray will be out for Sunday's game. Addison just had thumb surgery and won't play on Sunday while Murray won't be active either with his hamstring injury.

Cashman, Ingram-Dawkins, Hockenson, and Jauan Jennings are all on track to practice and play on Sunday.
